meta.scope: Argentina batch 4 — Provincial statistical offices + northern/NEA poorer-province contrast (homogeneity check). Covers Córdoba and Santa Fe (stronger provincial institutes) plus Chaco / Gran Resistencia and Formosa / Noreste region (higher poverty).
meta.homogeneity_note: Tests whether the State → Metro/capital → Local institute hierarchy remains usable outside the GBA and in higher-poverty northern provinces.

candidates.title: Provincia de Córdoba — core statistical identity
candidates.publisher: INDEC + Dirección General de Estadística y Censos de Córdoba
candidates.description: One of the largest and most economically diversified interior provinces. Strong provincial statistical office and a major urban agglomeration (Gran Córdoba).
candidates.notes: High-capacity interior province. Provincial statistical office is active and participates fully in the SEN. Useful contrast to both the GBA and the poorer northern provinces.

candidates.title: Dirección General de Estadística y Censos de la Provincia de Córdoba
candidates.publisher: Gobierno de la Provincia de Córdoba
candidates.description: Provincial statistical office that coordinates the Sistema Estadístico Provincial of Córdoba and produces or compiles provincial indicators under the SEN framework.
candidates.notes: One of the stronger provincial statistical services. Explicitly listed in SEN directories and maintains an active web presence.

candidates.title: Provincia de Santa Fe — core statistical identity
candidates.publisher: INDEC + Instituto Provincial de Estadística y Censos de Santa Fe (IPEC)
candidates.description: Major agricultural and industrial province with two large agglomerations (Gran Rosario, Gran Santa Fe). Active provincial statistical institute.
candidates.notes: Another high-capacity interior province. IPEC is a well-established provincial statistical body within the SEN.

candidates.title: Instituto Provincial de Estadística y Censos de Santa Fe (IPEC)
candidates.publisher: Gobierno de la Provincia de Santa Fe
candidates.description: Provincial statistical institute responsible for coordinating and producing official statistics for Santa Fe under the SEN architecture.
candidates.notes: Strong provincial counterpart to IDECBA and the Córdoba DGEC. Maintains public statistical products and participates in national operatives.

candidates.title: Provincia del Chaco — core statistical identity (northern/NEA contrast)
candidates.publisher: INDEC + Dirección de Estadística y Censos de Chaco
candidates.description: Northeastern province with persistently high poverty indicators. Gran Resistencia is one of the highest-poverty large agglomerations in recent EPH cuts. Tests the statistical hierarchy under higher marginalisation.
candidates.notes: Homogeneity-test province. Second-semester 2025 EPH: Gran Resistencia showed poverty of ~42.2% of persons and indigency ~13.2% — among the highest of the 31 agglomerations. Local statistical office exists but independent primary production is thinner; most usable series remain national cuts.

candidates.title: Gran Resistencia — municipal / agglomeration statistical profile
candidates.description: Principal urban agglomeration of Chaco and one of the highest-poverty large urban areas in the EPH sample. Data almost entirely from national programmes (EPH, census, IPC regional) with limited independent local packaging.
referenced_by: EPH labour and poverty results for the agglomeration
candidates.notes: Northern/NEA contrast node. High poverty and indigency relative to CABA or Córdoba. Demonstrates that the national statistical framework reaches the agglomeration, but local statistical density is low.

candidates.title: Provincia de Formosa — core statistical identity (northern/NEA contrast)
candidates.description: Northeastern border province with elevated poverty indicators relative to the national average. Part of the Noreste statistical region in EPH and IPC publications.
candidates.notes: Second northern contrast province. Recent EPH: Formosa agglomeration poverty ~27.9% of persons (still above national urban average in many periods). Local statistical capacity is thinner; reliance on INDEC frameworks is high.

candidates.title: Región Noreste (NEA) — statistical region in EPH / IPC
candidates.description: Statistical region used by INDEC for EPH, poverty and some price publications. Comprises Chaco, Corrientes, Formosa and Misiones. Regularly shows higher poverty and indigency than the national urban average.
referenced_by: Poverty and indigency incidence by statistical region
candidates.notes: Useful higher-level regional node for the northern homogeneity check. Second-semester 2025: Noreste poverty ~32.7% of persons, indigency ~7.5%. Gran Resistencia pulls the regional average up.

candidates.title: Dirección de Estadística y Censos de la Provincia del Chaco
candidates.publisher: Gobierno de la Provincia del Chaco
candidates.description: Provincial statistical service of Chaco. Exists within the SEN but with thinner independent publication cadence than Córdoba, Santa Fe or CABA institutes.
candidates.notes: Homogeneity test: the office exists and is listed in SEN directories, yet most high-frequency and poverty indicators used analytically remain the national EPH/IPC cuts. Local packaging capacity is limited.

candidates.title: Dirección de Estadística de la Provincia de Tucumán
candidates.publisher: Gobierno de la Provincia de Tucumán
candidates.description: Provincial statistical office (one of the older ones, founded 1881). Produces provincial indicators and participates in national operatives; also publishes local products such as the Canasta de Crianza.
candidates.notes: Noroeste example with a long-standing provincial office and some original local products (e.g. Canasta de Crianza). Still operates inside the SEN framework and relies heavily on national survey infrastructure.

proposed_edges.basis: Provincial statistical office is a component of the SEN under Ley 17.622.
IPEC is the provincial statistical service of Santa Fe within the SEN.
Gran Resistencia is the principal urban agglomeration of Chaco.
Labour and poverty indicators for the agglomeration come from the EPH geographic cuts.
Noreste is one of the statistical regions for which poverty and indigency are regularly tabulated.
Chaco provincial statistical service is listed within the SEN architecture.
Tucumán Dirección de Estadística operates as a provincial service of the SEN.
